correctness.rationale: For every k>=0 and 0<a<b, factorially reweighted positive tail ratios parameterize exactly the all-exponential-moment class with ratios in [a,b]. The quadratic bias shifts this sequence by one index after normalization; dominated convergence ensures the parameterization is a homeomorphism from a compact product topology to the total-variation topology. Shift conjugacy yields all cycles, dense periodic laws, infinite entropy, an explicit universal binary omega-limit example, and necessity/sufficiency of Bessel and periodic attraction. The quantitative TV bound follows from a pointwise (1±epsilon)^n weight sandwich and a normalization L1 inequality. Code checks finite examples and algebra independently, not infinite claims. Iid full-support ratio sequences have dense shift orbits almost surely by the second Borel–Cantelli lemma applied to disjoint occurrences of each cylinder from a countable basis.

value.rationale: The 2026 original Bessel-bias fixed-point map raises a natural stability issue: iterating to improve approximation may or may not converge. The theorem determines the entire invariant compact dynamical system, realizes all finite periods and even infinite-entropy symbolic dynamics despite positive super-factorial tails, and supplies an iff Bessel-attraction and asymptotic-cycle criterion with a quantitative total-variation bound. This is a complete structural classification for a motivated natural distributional transformation, not a mere isolated parameter substitution, small numerical gain or finite-table recalculation. Under a natural iid full-support ratio law, a dense orbit is almost sure rather than an isolated pathological construction.
